title: DocuLink Financial Statement Values v1
description: Financial numbers, percentages, dates, and structured financial-statement notes and filing items detected from text geometry. Coordinates use normalized displayed-page, top-left-origin 0–1 space.

notes.description: Canonical document-level footnote catalogue. One item is emitted per normalized note identifier; continuation headings are occurrences of the same note, never duplicate catalogue entries.

noteReferences.description: Narrative citations linked to the canonical note catalogue. A citation naming several notes produces one reference per identifier, sharing the source text and bounds.

items.description: Canonical document-level catalogue of filing items ("Item 1A. Risk Factors"). One entry per item, built from the table of contents and from the headings in the body, whichever the document supplies.

itemReferences.description: Narrative citations linked to the canonical item catalogue. An identifier absent from the catalogue is never published, which is what keeps "Item 601 of Regulation S-K" out of this array.

normalizedValue.description: Exact canonical decimal for numbers/percentages, or ISO-like value for unambiguous dates. Never a binary float.

magnitude.description: Multiplier expressed by a modifier attached directly to this number. normalizedValue already includes this multiplier.

segments.description: Physical click regions when a logical value wraps across lines or pages. bounds remains the first segment; each segment creates the full logical value while drawing only its own rectangle.

Heading.description: One physical occurrence of a complete heading, for a note or for a filing item. A continuation occurrence remains attached to its canonical catalogue entry rather than creating a second one.

segments.description: Physical lines of a wrapped heading, in reading order. bounds encloses all segments on the page.

Note.description: One canonical financial-statement note, keyed by a normalized integer, decimal or Roman-numeral identifier.

description.description: Canonical heading description without the Note identifier or continuation marker. Empty only when no heading supplies one.

NoteReference.description: One note identifier cited by narrative text and linked to its canonical catalogue entry.

description.description: Canonical description resolved from the note catalogue.

text.description: The complete citation as printed, including an explicit description when present.

descriptionPresent.description: True when the printed citation supplied a description; false when description was resolved only from the catalogue.

sourceDescription.description: Description printed in the citation. Present only when descriptionPresent is true.

ItemTocEntry.description: One row of a table of contents naming a filing item. The row is assembled from the lines sharing its band, so its cells are the segments: the identifier, the description, and the page number the document prints for it.

pageIndex.description: The page the contents row is printed on, not the page it points at.

text.description: The row as printed, cells joined in reading order.

printedPage.description: The page number printed in the row, exactly as printed. Absent when the row carries none.

corroborated.description: True when a detected table covered this row and supplied the column bands that classified its cells. False when the row was assembled from text geometry alone, which is how a contents page that table detection did not resolve still yields items.

segments.description: The row's cells, in reading order. bounds encloses all of them.

Item.description: One canonical filing item, keyed by its normalized identifier -- "7", "1A", "2.02". The key includes the part only when the same identifier appears under more than one part, which is what keeps a 10-Q's Part I Item 1 distinct from its Part II Item 1. At least one of headers or tocEntries is non-empty.

part.description: The Roman numeral of the part this item falls under, when the document groups items into parts. Absent when it does not.

description.description: Canonical item description without the Item identifier. Empty only when neither the contents nor a heading supplies one.

descriptionSource.description: Where description came from. The table of contents is the document's own index and wins over a body heading when the two disagree.

headers.description: Occurrences of this item's heading in the body. Empty when the item is listed in the contents but its heading was never found.

tocEntries.description: Contents rows naming this item. Empty when the document has no contents, or when the item is missing from it -- a body-only "Item 6. [Reserved]" is still catalogued.

ItemReference.description: One item identifier cited by narrative text and linked to its canonical catalogue entry.

part.description: The part named by the citation itself, as in "Part II, Item 7". Absent when the citation names no part.

description.description: Canonical description resolved from the item catalogue.

text.description: The complete citation as printed, including an explicit description when present.

descriptionPresent.description: True when the printed citation supplied a description; false when description was resolved only from the catalogue. A citation may name a subsection rather than the item's own title, so sourceDescription is not expected to match description.

sourceDescription.description: Description printed in the citation. Present only when descriptionPresent is true.

NoiseValue.description: A text span classified as non-linkable diagnostic noise. Most entries are recognized values later refused by evidence, while structured headings, contents rows and references are captured as complete text spans. Noise is never a click target.

reason.description: The classification group for this noise span. A new group is added here before it is implemented.

noise.description: Text spans this page classified as noise. Absent or empty when nothing was refused or classified. These are diagnostics, not values — no consumer may treat them as linkable.
